Verified: (1) Across all 64 operations, only raitPoolClaimNext, raitClaimContext and raitCaseRiskSnapshot changed. `components` is byte-identical between a3bd2df7 and f1cefdb8. The diff is info, the claim ETag/x-rait-scope text and the per-code error variants. The hashes recorded for the commands OpenAPI, both provenance-format files, source-review-disposition.md and source-freeze.md match both f1cefdb8 and the current tree. No later commit touches docs/framework or the ADRs. (2) F1: the retained claim POST codes now carry exactly their catalogued optional contexts: VALIDATION_FAILED fields[]; FORBIDDEN_ACTION resource/action/roles; FORBIDDEN_CASE_SCOPE caseId/poolId/unitId; QUEUE_EMPTY poolId; IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY key; ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_ACTIVE assignmentId/memberId; MEMBER_NOT_AVAILABLE memberId/availability/status; PARAMETER_SOURCE_PENDING key; ASSIGNMENT_WIP_LIMIT wip/limit; AUTH_REQUIRED and TENANT_MISMATCH empty. ORDER_OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN 403 with empty context is restored; it is emitted by existing runtime at rait-case-command.service.ts:809 and asserted at behavioral-matrix.spec.ts:1444. CASE_POOL_UNRESOLVED, CLAIM_LEGACY_UNVERIFIED and RISK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE stay empty-context. The status/messageKey envelope fields match catalogue §1. Every context field is optional and the descriptions forbid disclosing other candidates, so no read grant is created. (3) F2: productionBindings sets existingAcceptedImmutableVerifier=null and behavior=missing for all eight kinds: timer/track/movement/interruption/parameter/incident/applicability → 503, legacy → 409. productionBindingBoundary allows the synthetic tenant reader to replace only the provenance port, with the real SqlRaitRiskSnapshotFactory still running. Neither a digest, a label nor INF_RAIT_CASE_ADMIT creates authority. (4) F3: unshiftedCeilingQualification compares raw_due_on and due_on separately against the canonical expected values, requires clock.ceiling_on=due_on and returns 503 on any suspension/extension/adjustment. It adds no step shifting and no elapsed heuristic in the pure evaluator. Expected values can be computed through public owners: computeDue for catalogue durations, addCalendarDays/addCalendarMonths and Calendar.isBusinessDay/nextBusinessDay. (5) F4: info.version is 1.3.0 and the description and x-rait-scope state the S2 additions. (6) F5: the ETag description keeps the JARI/CETRAN v+1 unchanged; no event schema was invented. (7) F6: the storage spec (755421d4) authors UPDATE/DELETE denial, including an updated_at UPDATE denial at line 166, as schema-pending. (8) Clarifications: inf.ait_ait is the actual table, and every rowFields column of the 17 existing tables exists in the DDL. The rait_claim_legacy_qualification fieldset equals the blueprint entity minus the generator's updated_at. The applicability kind's only meaning is B / defesa_previa / not_applicable, with no clock or timer row and missing → 503. ORIGINAL start (authenticated disposition with coverage checkpoint) is kept distinct from RESET (authorized interruption plus a complete qualified policy). The legacy kind binds same-tenant case, admission (INF_RAIT_CASE_ADMIT plus its event), distribution history, pool scope, assignment and auth.users reviewer, and requires an independently admitted receipt located by receipt:<uuid>. No distribution audit action is invented. No remaining material source contradiction found.

findings.detail: The F1 correction also widened the error contexts of the two new GET operations, which the F1 disposition ('No other command') did not discuss. The raitCaseRiskSnapshot and raitClaimContext 403 FORBIDDEN_CASE_SCOPE variants now allow optional caseId/poolId/unitId (catalogue row 79 lists /casos/:id), where a3bd2df7 allowed only wip/limit. The existing S1 case-scope rejection emits an empty context (rait-case-command.service.ts:626). On the risk GET, poolId/unitId of an out-of-scope case would disclose where an unauthorized case is routed. Only the description prose ('caller/authorized own resource only') prevents this, not the schema.
findings.recommendation: Inspector HTTP assertions for both GETs should require that an out-of-scope or foreign case/pool returns FORBIDDEN_CASE_SCOPE or TENANT_MISMATCH with empty context, or at most the caller-supplied identifier. Optionally, as a later Architect maintenance item, narrow the GET 403 case-scope context to empty. Fields are optional, so this is not a blocking contradiction.

findings.detail: RaitClaimNextInput is {additionalProperties:false, properties:{}}, which implies 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for any field. The restored 403 ORDER_OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN variant keeps the existing runtime precedence: caseId in the body → 403, checked before the field allowlist (service.ts:809), as asserted by behavioral-matrix.spec.ts:1444. The contract does not state that a body containing caseId gets 403 rather than schema-level 400. ADR-0045 item 3 says only 'rejecting ... selected-case fields'.
findings.recommendation: Inspector should keep the existing precedence explicitly (caseId → 403 ORDER_OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN with no effects; other unknown or server-owned fields → 400). Engineer must not put a generic schema validator in front of that check. No source change is required.

findings.detail: Pending Engineer reconciliation of existing claim error emission with the corrected contract. In a race on a server-selected candidate those identifiers belong to another analyst, so the description's non-disclosure rule makes them effectively non-emittable on claim-next. This is runtime work still pending, not a source contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Inspector should assert PARAMETER_SOURCE_PENDING without poolId, and ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_ACTIVE / FORBIDDEN_CASE_SCOPE on claim-next without another actor's assignment, member or case identifiers. Engineer aligns emission at GREEN. Classified as pending.

findings.detail: F3 implementability check for the A-360 track. The engine has no existing writer for a 360-day T-DEC timer: T-DEC catalogue durationValue=180, EXTENDABLE={T-DIL} only, and computeDue(T-DEC) always yields start+180. The expected 360 raw due is still computable through public owners: exported addCalendarDays plus forward rounding with the public Calendar, which matches the private roundForward. So the rule is consistent. Combined with productionBindings=missing, an A-360 positive can exist only in controlled fixtures.
findings.recommendation: Engineer must not use computeDue(T-DEC) as the 360 expectation, call private rawDueFor, or treat extension_count>0 as the 360 track. Inspector precomputes 180 and 360 raw/due separately, including a non-business-day rounding case. No source change.
